items.title: 68089_John Malachi oral history interview
items.q: We were in St. Louis, and Art Blakey arrived and then came in, and we had a rehearsal.

ctx.x: finally, he came to, us when we were in Kansas City, and said, "Well, when we get to St. Louis, I've got this cat coming in that's from Pittsburgh. He's with Fletcher Henderson's band now. His name is Art Blakey." So I'd never met Art before, and some of the guys knew Art. And I think it was at that particular time, one of the trumpet players, I believe, had... Let's see. No, no. I'm getting ahead of my story.

We were in St. Louis, and Art Blakey arrived and then came in, and we had a rehearsal. I never will forget, in the first rehearsal, we rehearsed some tune... By this time, with everyone writing, we had acquired I guess about 17 or 18 arrangements. Because all during the tour, everybody was writing something.

Anyway, as I said before, Dizzy was the straw boss, and he kicked off this first number with Art Blakey, and we started playing and all of a sudden, Art went into kind of a shuffle rhythm. And Dizzy, his way of stopping the band was, he'd always whistle and wave his hands and say, "Stop, stop, stop the band!" And he pointed at Art Blakey and he said, "Look, don't you ever play like that again as long as you live." Well, everybody laughed, you know. So he told him what he wanted. And Dizzy can play very good…
